./docs/evidence/deployments/retired-docs-source-5d5544d0.json:14:      "text": "---\ndocument_type: app-readme\nlifecycle: current\nauthority: canonical\nowner: taxkit-docs-app-owner\nlast_reviewed: 2026-10-06\nreview_trigger: docs route, content boundary, build target, runtime, credential source, proof or deployment ownership change\n---\n\n# Docs app\n\nThe app and script typechecks select ESNext modules to support the compiler\nconfiguration's explicit JSON import declaration under Node's native loader.\nThe docs-content README owns that shared configuration contract.\n\nThis private TanStack Start app renders the public TaxKit developer\ndocumentation.\n\nIt owns routes, the app shell, navigation presentation, app-local MDX component\ncomposition and browser rendering. It does not own canonical docs schemas,\nvalidation policy or generated Fumadocs source access; those live in\n`@taxkit/docs-content`. Reusable Fumadocs integration lives in\n`@taxkit/docs-fumadocs`.\n\n## Content root\n\nPublic MDX content lives in:\n\n```txt\npackages/docs-content/content\n```\n\nEach top-level section owns an `index.mdx` file. Later content tasks can add\nchild pages below the matching section directory.\n\n## Navigation contract\n\nThe public docs navigation is defined in:\n\n```txt\npackages/docs-content/navigation.json\n```\n\nThe required top-level sections are:\n\n- Start\n- SDK\n- API\n- Guides\n- Concepts\n- Contributing\n- Reference\n\nThe navigation file is the source of truth for sidebar order until a docs\nruntime owns a generated or typed navigation API. It is decoded and validated\nby `@taxkit/docs-content`.\n\n## Runtime graph\n\n```ts\nProduction: docs page\n\nbrowser\n  -> TanStack route loader\n    -> createServerFn\n      -> dynamic .server module\n        -> one app-owned ManagedRuntime\n          -> DocsContentService + DocsRuntimeProbe\n            -> @taxkit/docs-content live layer\n              -> @taxkit/docs-fumadocs FumadocsSource\n              -> TaxKit generated collection adapter\n              -> packages/docs-content/.source/server\n              -> schema-decoded navigation.json representation\n        -> schema-encoded Exit representation\n    -> TanStack SSR hydration or client-navigation transport\n      -> direct route-root restore and Result match\n        -> @taxkit/docs-content/client\n          -> Fumadocs compiled MDX module\n        -> @taxkit/docs-fumadocs/render\n        -> app-local MDX component map\n```\n\n## Commands\n\n```txt\nbun run --filter=docs dev\nbun run --filter=docs dev:vite\nbun run --filter=docs check-import-boundaries\nbun run --filter=docs test\nbun run --filter=docs test:imports\nbun run --filter=docs test:browser\nbun run --filter=docs test:built\nbun run --filter=docs test:cloudflare-built\nbun run --filter=docs test:cloudflare-hosted\nbun run --filter=docs test:scripts\nbun run --filter=docs build:cloudflare\nbun run --filter=docs check-types\nbun run --filter=docs build\nbun run --filter=docs preview\nbun run --filter=@taxkit/docs-examples check-examples\nbun run docs:validate\n```\n\n`dev` is the authoritative Alchemy-managed Cloudflare development path. The\nroot adapter selects Doppler project/config `taxkit/dev`, strips ambient\nDoppler and Cloudflare values, disables Doppler fallback and both Bun and\nAlchemy `.env` loading, and then runs the source-neutral internal `alchemy dev`\ncommand. Alchemy's local `dev_<user>` stage is decoded separately; Preview and\nProduction inputs and evidence remain limited to `pr-N` or `prod`. Run\n`bun run check:doppler-custody` after the repository-scoped login described in\nthe [deployment runbook](../../docs/runbooks/docs-deployment.md). A successful\nlocal start does not grant provider authority or prove a deployment.\n\n`dev:vite` is the fast, infrastructure-free portless Vite path at\n`https://docs.taxkit.localhost`.\nAlchemy beta.80 injects its Cloudflare Vite plugin for the native resource;\nstandalone Vite installs the same official plugin only when the documented\n`ALCHEMY_CLOUDFLARE_VITE_INJECTED` guard is absent.\n\n`@taxkit/docs-examples` owns the four public integration templates. Its\n`check-types` and `check-examples` check their current SDK/API/calculator\nexports; content validation checks their source links.\n\nRun `build` before `preview`. Turbo orders the package-owned content build\nbefore the app, while a direct Vite app build regenerates the same package-owned\nsource through `source.config.ts`. The config-only Fumadocs export is\nsource-owned, so a clean direct app build does not require a prebuilt workspace\nartifact. The Vite config resolves the Fumadocs config and generated-source\npaths from its own file location, so the standalone and repository-root\nAlchemy builds use the same generated source even after a cached package\nbuild. Fumadocs MDX 15 supplies its native plugin array; the old single-plugin\n`buildStart` wrapper is removed. Local build and browser checks qualify this\ngenerator change separately from any provider artifact. `dev:vite` and `preview` expose the app through portless.\n\nThe default docs test command runs the native import-checker fixtures, the\nnative route-result and managed-runtime tests, the existing MDX link tests and\nthe built/hosted-proof policy and real browser adapter fixtures. The server test configuration resolves both\nordinary and server imports to package source. Route fixtures use the owning\nSchemas and native Effect encoders; no test-local Promise runner or throwing\ncodec is required. Managed-runtime tests acquire and dispose the actual factory\ninside a scope, including failed and interrupted requests. These tests prove\nlocal lifetime and representation behaviour, separate from Worker/browser proof.\n\n`test:browser` runs the programmatic TanStack client-route harness in Chromium.\nIts native Effect tests scope the DOM host, React root, router history and\nconsole spies. Only its fake server-function loader executes an Effect; test\nbodies use the native runner. The browser test configuration is included in\nboth the compiler and unused-code inventories.\nIt proves success, expected failures, malformed transport and framework error\nboundaries after `Route.useLoaderData`; it does not prove SSR or hydration. Use\nthe built app for initial SSR, hydration and real client-navigation proof.\n\n`test:built` builds the production Cloudflare Worker/assets output and executes\nthe generated no-bundle Worker through a command-owned local workerd server. It\nasserts a known page in the HTTP response before browser JavaScript, hydration\nwithout warnings or errors, real sidebar and authored-MDX client transitions\nwith zero document requests, browser back/forward, heading focus without\nstealing initial-hydration focus, pending state, framework-native client\nnot-found behavior and a direct HTTP 404. It also checks the skip link,\nlandmarks, labelled/current navigation, mobile disclosure, representative\ncontrast, reduced-motion rendering, immutable asset headers, runtime reuse,\nfilesystem isolation and compressed upload size. The command owns\nbrowser/workerd cleanup. Its native Command entry calls the closed\n`LocalCloudflareBuiltProof` service; Playwright objects stay inside its private\nadapter. Config acquires only the existing allowlisted local environment, and\nnative filesystem, HTTP, Crypto and child-process streams own the work. Each\noutput pipe has a 1 MiB limit; generated artifact reads have a 64 MiB limit and\n10,000-file ceiling. Sorted path/NUL/file bytes/NUL digests retain the previous\nartifact identity. One five-minute deadline covers the entire operation, with\na two-minute browser limit. Scoped cleanup completes before the whole owning\nreceipt Schema is encoded, saved and read back. Requested screenshot cardinality\nand both receipt/manifest readbacks are checked. `test:cloudflare-built` remains an explicit alias for\nthe same canonical proof command. Add `-- --screenshots` for the bounded\ncandidate-bound desktop/mobile PNG and digest manifest under ignored\n`tmp/docs-cloudflare/`. The desktop capture shows the representative guide;\nthe mobile capture shows its open navigation state. Screenshot review\nsupplements these behavioral assertions and cannot prove request type, focus\nbehavior, contrast, motion suppression, HTTP status, hydration, console\ncleanliness or hosted behavior.\n\n`build` and its compatibility alias `build:cloudflare` select the exact\nofficial Cloudflare Vite adapter and emit the deployable no-bundle Worker at\n`dist/server/index.js` plus `dist/client` assets. The canonical built proof\nstrips provider credentials from the child environment, performs a Wrangler\ndry-run, and runs an isolated output-only copy under real workerd. It reuses the\nbuilt-app behavioral contract for SSR, assets, server functions, 404,\nhydration, no-document navigation, accessibility and console cleanliness, and\nadds concurrent-isolate, filesystem, binding, compressed-upload-size, local\nreadiness-timing and immutable asset-header oracles. The local timing is not a\nCloudflare CPU-startup-limit receipt. The exact verified invocation is:\n\n```sh\nbun run --filter=docs test:cloudflare-built\n```\n\nThis is local workerd evidence only. It does not prove Alchemy state, a\nCloudflare deployment, a `workers.dev` URL, Preview, Production or rollback.\nThe former docs-app Nitro/Vercel bridge has been removed after local parity;\nNitro remains an independent owner only where another application still uses\nit. Final hosted requalification of the exact retirement candidate and the\nreport-only Alchemy state boundary remain separate claims.\n\nRoot `alchemy.run.ts` composes the private\n`@taxkit/infrastructure` declaration of\n`Cloudflare.Website.Vite(\"DocsWebsite\")`. Alchemy owns Vite build execution,\nassets, the SSR Worker lifecycle and the physical Worker name as one logical\nresource. Its beta.80 memo includes the lockfile and both sibling docs\npackages, so those authored inputs participate in Alchemy's resource input.\nThe standalone `build:cloudflare` alias and workerd harness are provider-free\npreflight proof; their `dist/**` output is not asserted to be the exact artifact\nproduced inside an Alchemy plan/apply. `.wrangler/**` and `dist/**` remain\nignored generated output and are never deployment receipts.\n\nPreview and exact-stage teardown repository source selects only\n`taxkit/stg_preview` through the shared Preview GitHub environment. Preview\nselects `taxkit/ci` separately for its two Turbo consumers after cache saves;\nteardown does not fetch it. Their upload steps receive only a separately\nprepared allowlist of sanitised proof files, while raw provider output stays on\nthe runner. Production uses its separate protected `taxkit/prd` bridge, fixed\n`prod` stage and the same allowlisted upload owner. No hosted Doppler fetch is\nclaimed before the separately approved TaxKit bridge is created and read back.\n\nExact Preview, Production, teardown, rollback and Alchemy-state operations\nbelong to `docs/runbooks/docs-deployment.md`; dated sanitized observations\nbelong below `docs/evidence/deployments/`. The hosted harness requires the\nread-back URL, candidate, stage, environment, plan/config/lock/deployment-input\ndigests, Worker/deployment/version identities, evidence directory and rollback\nidentity. Effect Config and the owning Schemas decode those values plus the\nwhole-number retry count and delay before Chromium starts. Preview must pair\n`pr-N` with the same positive PR number; Production and rollback must pair\n`prod` with no PR number. Missing, empty, partial-number, unsafe-path and\nsecret-bearing URL input fails with a value-free tagged error. Checked account,\nprovider, stage, evidence-directory, URL, commit and hash values have distinct\nSchema-owned branded types; their encoded text stays unchanged. The named `CloudflareHostedProof` service keeps Playwright objects private in\nits live Layer. The command validates Workers URLs and deployment metadata\nbefore starting a browser; controlled adapter tests additionally use an exact\nloopback origin. Its native operations own browser and listener cleanup,\nHTTP/body reads, filesystem and Crypto. Optional input becomes Option internally\nand retains the historical null JSON fields. The complete observation has an\nowning Schema, separate from the workflow's required-field admission projection.\n\nThe docs package test task and root docs-boundary test task both retain and\nhash `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` through Turbo. A native check reads the actual\ntask settings so direct and full-graph tests use the same installed browser.\nThe hosted operation has one five-minute deadline. Browser event callbacks only\nwrite to a bounded native Queue; overflow fails the proof rather than dropping\nwarnings silently. Scoped Ref updates keep immutable observations. A hydration\nretry still requires an observed same-site 404 for a hashed JavaScript asset,\nretains the configured attempt limit and clears only that failed attempt's\ndiagnostics. Other browser failures stop immediately. The command writes the\nsame candidate-qualified desktop/mobile PNGs and emits the same identity and\nbehaviour fields. Malformed server-function input uses raw bytes: Playwright\nJSON-encodes a string when its content type is JSON, which would otherwise send\na valid JSON string instead of broken JSON.\n\nNative policy tests cover invalid settings, stage identity, success/failure/\ninterruption cleanup, safe errors, complete output and absent optional metadata.\nReal Chromium fixtures cover temporary/permanent missing assets, unrelated\nprivate diagnostics, missing hydration, Queue overflow, and interruption of a\npending streaming response. A controlled HTTP/DOM fixture exercises the complete\nnamed operation, navigation, readable text, focus, mobile menu, actual screenshot\nfiles and malformed request bytes. These are local adapter checks; the fixture's\nruntime headers and HTML do not establish Worker or hosted behaviour.\nThe separate\ncredential-free Production hosted verification workflow can recheck an\nalready deployed Worker using reviewed, dated evidence; it does not apply or\nroll back a Worker.\n\nThe first dated Preview observation was torn down but did not meet the final\nevidence contract, so it remains disconfirming history. Fresh candidate\n`d9cb894…` passed the corrected hosted, screenshot and pre-mutation contracts,\nindependent adversarial review and full repository gates and was then torn\ndown; DCD-002\nis accepted. DCD-003 then deployed that source to fixed `prod`, qualified\n`c99984c…` through Preview and Production, removed the successor Preview, and\nrestored `d9cb894…` through the same normal Alchemy graph. The current\ndated Production readback observed one stable Worker URL and restored\nsource-bound state; it does not establish timeless availability. This does not\nclaim byte promotion, recovery from known broken content, a custom domain/DNS\nroute, a paid plan or release/publication.\n\nThe import checker runs through its exact Bun command entrypoint and native\nEffect FileSystem/Path services. It lists source files, skips server/test/generated\nowners and non-file entries, inspects direct static imports/exports with the\npinned TypeScript 6 compatibility parser, and rejects browser runtime use or\na `runtime.client.ts` file. Read/list/stat failures fail the command with safe\noperation labels. This source check is separate from the built browser bundle\nand Worker checks; it does not establish the complete transitive import graph.\n\n`test:imports` runs native Effect fixtures for browser-safe source, forbidden\nreferences, ignored owners, an empty runtime file and file-service failures.\nThe default `test` command includes this corpus; `check-types` includes the\nchecker, fixtures and their test configuration. These exact files receive the\ncanonical strict rules, with only the command entrypoint allowed to execute\nan application. Canonical rules also cover all docs app source and its Vite,\nserver-test and browser-test configurations. The source permits execution only\nat the exact Worker, server-loader, runtime factory and fake browser-loader\nowners. Other docs proof-script migration work remains with DEV-73.\n\n`check-import-boundaries` rejects server-only content, service, generated-source\nand runtime imports from browser-reachable app modules. The docs app has no\nbrowser Effect runtime. Its `.server.ts` loader module is the only route edge\nthat acquires `DocsContentService`, and the module-scoped server runtime is\nreused for the server isolate. The same runtime owns a private live\n`DocsRuntimeProbe` Layer. That Layer acquires one Effect `Ref` construction\nstate and an identifier produced by Effect `Random`; focused tests inject an\nexact deterministic identifier and dispose the complete runtime. The runtime\nfactory exposes disposal so tests and future host lifecycle integration can\nrelease all Layers; the current hosting adapter does not provide an\napplication shutdown hook.\n\nThe Worker entry accepts the exact\n`x-taxkit-docs-runtime-proof: construction-count` opt-in header and returns a\nnon-secret construction count plus random isolate identifier. The host callback\nruns one native Effect at the Worker entry, normalising the framework's\n`Response | Promise<Response>` result there. It uses the request's abort signal\nfor that Effect; this does not establish cancellation inside the framework's\npromise. Ordinary responses do not initialise documentation services. An\nopt-in request acquires the existing application runtime's cached context for\nthe typed probe read, and Schema-encodes it at response-header egress. It\nreplaces only the two proof headers and preserves other response headers,\nbody and status; it owns no counter or randomness itself. This\ntemporary deployment-migration channel proves reuse within the observed\nprocess/isolate across requests; it is not a public API and does not prove a\nsingleton across Cloudflare isolates. Review it when the runtime, Worker entry,\nprivacy boundary or proof channel changes. Retire it after an equally strong\nnon-public provider oracle exists; otherwise retain its bounded\none-identifier/two-header carrying cost explicitly through migration parity.\n\nThe app-local MDX adapter classifies root-relative, query-only and authored\nrelative `.mdx` destinations as TanStack routes while keeping external,\nprotocol-relative, mail, download, repository-source and same-document\ndestinations as anchors. It removes an authored `.mdx` suffix before any query\nor fragment without changing either suffix. Sidebar, home and MDX route links\nset one app-owned navigation-focus intent; the destination heading consumes it\nafter a client transition. Initial hydration does not set that intent. 138	## Patch-free Alchemy design
   139	
   140	TaxKit currently locks Effect 4.0.0 and patched Alchemy 2.0.0-beta.80. Common
   141	Practice locks Effect 4.0.2 and unpatched Alchemy 2.0.0-beta.81. The target is the
   142	compatible, published, unpatched upstream package used by Common Practice,
   143	checked against TaxKit's installed types and consumers during implementation.
   144	An upstream comparison is not an installation or a completed upgrade.
   145	
   146	Two declarations need to change before removing the current Alchemy patch:
   147	
   148	1. **Remove the two-way output dependency.** In
   149	   `packages/infrastructure/src/apps-stack.ts`, Website uses API output/binding
   150	   while API reads Website output. Replace API's reverse dependency with one
   151	   checked, stage-owned exact Website address. The same settings own its domain
   152	   or checked Worker name. For Preview, retain the actual existing Worker name
   153	   and use Alchemy's native checked account-subdomain setting; do not guess the
   154	   generated hostname or add Preview DNS as an incidental change. API retains
   155	   its own `Worker.URL`; Website consumes
   156	   API output and retains its own `Worker.URL`. Declare API, then Website.
   157	   Confirm native local development addresses before implementation: local ports
   158	   can be assigned at runtime. Do not widen allowed Origins to `*` or infer an
   159	   address from arbitrary request headers to solve this.
   160	2. **Avoid the shared redirect write.** Remove `domain.redirects` from the
   161	   Website declaration. Attach the native apex and `www` domain aliases to the
   162	   Website, then return the existing permanent redirect to the canonical apex
   163	   at Website ingress, before routes or calculator forms. Preserve path/query
   164	   semantics and the current redirect status. This bypasses the Worker
   165	   provider's shared-zone redirect ruleset code without a custom provider.
   166	   Common Practice itself uses `domain.redirects`; this field is a necessary
   167	   TaxKit departure. Previously saved redirect declarations can invoke the
   168	   same provider path during removal, so check the existing-state transition
   169	   before calling the migration safe. No patched replacement is permitted.
   170	
   171	Upstream beta.81 still treats every shared redirect-rules read failure as an
   172	absent ruleset. The earlier mocked forbidden-read case produced a replacement
   173	write. That shows a problem with blindly keeping this declaration while deleting
   174	the patch; it does not require retaining the patch. A separate native Ruleset
   175	resource owns an entire zone phase, so it is unsuitable unless TaxKit owns every
   176	rule in that phase. Use the Website alias/redirect approach instead.
   177	
   178	Remove the Alchemy entry from `patchedDependencies`, its patch file, and the
   179	corresponding lockfile patch references together. Search build, install and
   180	infrastructure code for every other Alchemy modification. Do not relocate a fix
   181	into a wrapper, copied source or postinstall step. Preserve logical resource IDs,
   182	stack/state identities and the existing unrelated DNS records.
   183	
   184	The Atom scheduler peer-metadata patch is unrelated to Alchemy. Common Practice
   185	also has non-Alchemy Effect/PostHog patches; those are not required by this
   186	proposal and must not be copied without a TaxKit need. Align the Effect family
   187	and explicit companion override if choosing 4.0.2. Any React/Atom compatibility
   188	change needs ordinary type/build/browser checks, not a new exception receipt.
   189	
   190	## Ordinary commits, deployments and Doppler
   191	
   192	Copy Common Practice's workflow shape:
   193	
   194	- Make normal coherent Git commits and PRs. Describe the change and meaningful
   208	- Use native `Doppler.Secrets`, `.env` and disabled `ProcessEnv` fallback in one
   209	  owner, following Common Practice. `.env` overrides also apply in hosted runs;
   210	  Actions should write deployment metadata only. Retain TaxKit's actual Doppler
   211	  project/config mapping and environment-scoped read-only Doppler credentials.
   212	  Do not copy another project's values or duplicate Cloudflare keys in GitHub.
   213	- Roll back by redeploying the previous working Git revision through the same
   214	  native workflow. Alchemy resource retention is not a deployment snapshot.
   215	
   216	Target scripts are short native commands such as `dev`, `pr:plan`, `pr:deploy`,
   217	`pr:destroy`, `production:plan`, `production:deploy` and `production:drift`.
   218	The names can match Common Practice while selecting TaxKit's existing `prod`
   219	and `pr-N` state identities. Do not rename a live stack/stage as a side effect
   220	of making commands prettier. Native local development still needs its exact
   221	address and state behaviour checked; delete custom wrappers once their useful
   222	behaviour is covered by the native entrypoint.
   223	
   224	GitHub records the commit and run; Alchemy records state; the smoke check
   225	confirms the deployed endpoints. No separate receipt workflow, deployment
   226	manifest, hash catalogue, custody packet or per-step approval file is needed.

   105	This resolves the Website choice for the foundation change. A later HTTP switch
   106	can be assessed on its own merit; it is not required to adopt Common Practice.
   107	
   108	## Cloudflare first, with host-independent packages
   109	
   110	Use Effect services and Layers to describe shared operations and supply their
   111	implementations. Core, rule, calculator and transport packages must not import
   112	Cloudflare, Alchemy or Bun server code, interpret trusted Cloudflare headers, or
   113	run Effects themselves. The SDK's private Promise adapter is a justified public
   114	library execution boundary.
   115	
   116	The API app owns the host adapters. Cloudflare supplies native request context,
   117	private bindings, rate services and sessions. Bun supplies its HTTP server and
   118	configuration through one top-level runner. Both use the same tax operations.
   119	Do not add a managed Promise runtime to the native API Worker.
   120	
   121	Matching upstream Effect 4.0.2 supports this separation: `HttpApiBuilder` captures
   122	shared services, `HttpRouter` supplies the current request scope, and
   123	`BunHttpServer` supplies the abstract server. `HttpRouter.provideRequest` builds
   124	its supplied Layer per request; it must not own an application-wide capacity
   125	pool. Alchemy's Worker bridge builds the application once and supplies native
   126	request context. Stream cleanup belongs to the current consumer; isolate
   127	shutdown is not a guaranteed cleanup hook.
   128	
   129	Cloudflare already captures one bounded calculation service. Keep its shared
   130	eight-place pool, five-second work budget, exact Website Origin and checked
   131	private identity. A timer cannot interrupt synchronous calculation code.
   132	
   133	Bun currently builds the bounded service per request, creating a fresh pool for
   134	each one. Fix that at Bun application composition after the Cloudflare work.
   135	Keep its current HTTP coverage and explicitly owned CORS/admission differences;
   136	no Cloudflare Durable Object substitute or new Bun protocol promise is needed.
   137	
   138	## Patch-free Alchemy design
   139	
   140	TaxKit currently locks Effect 4.0.0 and patched Alchemy 2.0.0-beta.80. Common
   141	Practice locks Effect 4.0.2 and unpatched Alchemy 2.0.0-beta.81. The target is the
   142	compatible, published, unpatched upstream package used by Common Practice,
   143	checked against TaxKit's installed types and consumers during implementation.
   144	An upstream comparison is not an installation or a completed upgrade.
   145	
   146	Two declarations need to change before removing the current Alchemy patch:
   147	
   148	1. **Remove the two-way output dependency.** In
   149	   `packages/infrastructure/src/apps-stack.ts`, Website uses API output/binding
   150	   while API reads Website output. Replace API's reverse dependency with one
   151	   checked, stage-owned exact Website address. The same settings own its domain
   152	   or checked Worker name. For Preview, retain the actual existing Worker name
   153	   and use the actual account subdomain through Alchemy's native setting; syntax
   154	   checks alone do not confirm account ownership. Do not guess the
   155	   generated hostname or add Preview DNS as an incidental change. API retains
   156	   its own `Worker.URL`; Website consumes API output and retains its own
   157	   `Worker.URL`. Declare API, then Website.
   158	   Use fixed local ports and `strictPort: true`, following Common Practice,
   159	   so an occupied port fails rather than silently changing the allowed origin.
   160	   Check both native local addresses before implementation. Do not widen allowed Origins to `*` or infer an
   161	   address from arbitrary request headers to solve this.
   162	2. **Avoid the shared redirect write.** Remove `domain.redirects` from the
   163	   Website declaration. Set the canonical `domain.name` to `taxkit.dev` and
   164	   `aliases` to `["www.taxkit.dev"]`. At Website ingress, return the existing
   165	   permanent redirect for `www` before routes or calculator forms. Select native
   166	   `assets: { runWorkerFirst: true }` so static files cannot skip that host check;
   167	   then serve canonical static files through the native `ASSETS` binding while
   168	   preserving the normal page fallback. The current Website needs this asset
   169	   delegation added. Preserve path/query semantics and the current redirect
   170	   status. This bypasses the Worker
   171	   provider's shared-zone redirect ruleset code without a custom provider.
   172	   Common Practice itself uses `domain.redirects`; this field is a necessary
   173	   TaxKit departure. Previously saved redirect declarations can invoke the
   174	   same provider path during removal, so check the existing-state transition
   175	   before calling the migration safe. No patched replacement is permitted.
   176	
   177	Upstream beta.81 still treats every shared redirect-rules read failure as an
   178	absent ruleset. The earlier mocked forbidden-read case produced a replacement
   179	write. That shows a problem with blindly keeping this declaration while deleting
   180	the patch; it does not require retaining the patch. A separate native Ruleset
   181	resource owns an entire zone phase, so it is unsuitable unless TaxKit owns every
   182	rule in that phase. Use the Website alias/redirect approach instead.
   183	
   184	Remove the Alchemy entry from `patchedDependencies`, its patch file, and the
   185	corresponding lockfile patch references together. Search build, install and
   186	infrastructure code for every other Alchemy modification. Do not relocate a fix
   187	into a wrapper, copied source or postinstall step. Preserve logical resource IDs,
   188	stack/state identities and the existing unrelated DNS records.

   108	## Cloudflare first, with host-independent packages
   109	
   110	Use Effect services and Layers to describe shared operations and supply their

   113	run Effects themselves. The SDK's private Promise adapter is a justified public
   114	library execution boundary.

   117	private bindings, rate services and sessions. Bun supplies its HTTP server and
   118	configuration through one top-level runner. Both use the same tax operations.
   119	Do not add a managed Promise runtime to the native API Worker.
   120

   122	shared services, `HttpRouter` supplies the current request scope, and
   123	`BunHttpServer` supplies the abstract server. `HttpRouter.provideRequest` builds
   124	its supplied Layer per request; it must not own an application-wide capacity
   125	pool. Alchemy's Worker bridge builds the application once and supplies native
   126	request context. Stream cleanup belongs to the current consumer; isolate
   127	shutdown is not a guaranteed cleanup hook.

---
name: grilling
description: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
---

Interview the user relentlessly until you reach a shared understanding. Map this as a **design tree**: every decision branches into the decisions that hang off it.
Work the tree in **rounds**. The **frontier** is every decision whose prerequisites are already settled: the questions you can ask _now_ without guessing at answers you haven't heard yet. Ask the whole frontier in one round: number each question and give your recommended answer. Then wait for the user's answers before the next round.

Format a round like so:

```
❓ **Q1** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>

➡️ <your recommended answer>

---
❓ **Q2** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>

➡️ <your recommended answer>
```

Each round the user answers reshapes the tree: settled decisions push the frontier outward and unblock questions that depended on them. Recompute the frontier and ask the next round. A question whose answer depends on another question still open in this round belongs to a _later_ round, not this one.
Finding _facts_ is your job, never the user's. When a frontier question needs a fact from the environment (filesystem, tools, etc.), dispatch a sub-agent to find it; don't ask the user for anything you could look up yourself. Don't block on it: a running exploration is an unsettled prerequisite, so only the questions downstream of it wait for the sub-agent to report; ask the rest of the frontier now. The _decisions_ are the user's: put each to them and wait.
The session is done when the frontier is empty: every branch of the design tree visited, nothing left silently assumed. Do not act on it until the user confirms you have reached a shared understanding.
---
name: repo-structure
description: Scaffold, audit, migrate, or validate a strict Bun and Turbo TypeScript monorepo with a TanStack Start app, Effect v4 domain/RPC/HTTP API packages, live-types export conditions, Oxlint/Oxfmt, Vitest, Knip, docs, CI, and repository-owned skills. Use for repository topology, root tooling, workspace contracts, current dependency snapshots, app/runtime composition, or a new repo using the separate Website/API architecture. Do not use for an isolated package inside an established repository.
---

# Repository Structure

Create a small repository whose boundaries are executable, documented, and
updateable. Resolve current versions first; render only from a recorded snapshot.

## Audit before scaffolding

1. Read `AGENTS.md`, all repository-owned readable `docs/**` and `README*`,
   manifests, workspace/lock/runtime config, lint/format/test/CI config, skills,
   and representative apps/packages. Exclude generated, dependency, build, and
   vendored trees explicitly.
2. Inspect worktree state. For an existing repository, patch only authorized
   paths and preserve unrelated work.
3. For an existing-repository audit, read the
   [repository audit router](references/repository-audit.md), then load its
   [workflow](references/audit/workflow.md),
   [corpus and journeys](references/audit/corpus-and-journeys.md),
   [lenses](references/audit/lenses.md),
   [findings and acceptance](references/audit/findings-and-acceptance.md), and
   [variation and stopping](references/audit/variation-and-stopping.md).
   Then read the
   [repository contract](references/repository-contract.md),
   [TanStack and Effect architecture](references/tanstack-effect.md), and
   [tooling and docs](references/tooling-and-docs.md).
4. Load the canonical sibling
   [`package-structure`](../package-structure/SKILL.md) and
   [`docs-maintainer`](../docs-maintainer/SKILL.md) skills. Resolve them
   relative to this installed skill collection, or pass the skill collection
   explicitly to the renderer. Stop before rendering if either is unavailable;
   do not invent package/document contracts or assume a user's home directory.

## Audit an existing repository

Default to report-first. Define the target revision, claimed jobs, accepted
outcomes, proof boundaries, authority, exclusions, and stop conditions. Account
for the repository corpus, then follow a small set of representative jobs from
request through ownership, implementation, proof, delivery, and acceptance.
Use prior collaboration evidence when available and authorized; treat it as
trajectory evidence rather than repository policy.

For a whole-repository audit, create the structured scope and finding artifacts
from `assets/audit/`; do not use free-form prose as the sole audit record.
Validate them with `scripts/validate_audit_artifacts.py`. Return a
consequence-ordered Markdown view with stable IDs, separate important
corrections from optional improvements, identify the earliest owning
correction, and name duplicated machinery to retire. Stop for acceptance before
implementation unless the original request authorizes both. Record accepted
finding IDs in the crosswalk, hand them to `prd-writer`, then use `prd-review`
and `prd-implementer`.

For most repositories, stop after the structural and trajectory audit,
accepted important corrections, normal repository checks, and one fresh
independent review. Do not create a comparative harness evaluation unless the
claim is that a particular intervention changes future worker behavior.

## Resolve or select versions

Rendering is offline and deterministic. The checked-in snapshot is a known-good
fallback, not permission to call it current. To research a refresh, use primary
registries/official sources and DeepWiki only for upstream packages—not the
local codebase:

```bash
python3 scripts/resolve_versions.py --output /tmp/provisional-versions.json
```

Effect ecosystem packages share the qualified exact stable v4 version, currently
`4.0.2`. Resolve that exact version; registry `latest`/`beta` tags do not
select the qualified native Alchemy combination. TanStack Start and Router
resolve independently. Never emit `latest`.
Alchemy beta and the preview-only Cloudflare scaffold require an explicit
qualified/rejected decision; never infer compatibility from a registry tag.
Read [version policy](references/version-policy.md); a snapshot is adopted only
after full compatibility rendering and verification.

## Render safely

The target must be an absolute, new path. There is no overwrite mode:

```bash
python3 scripts/render_repository.py \
  --target /absolute/new/repository \
  --name example \
  --scope @example \
  --source-condition @example/source \
  --versions assets/version-snapshot.json
```

The renderer stages root/app/docs/tooling assets, invokes the canonical package
renderer for domain, RPC, and HTTP API packages, copies every complete current
repository-skill folder, adds only the declared repository-local profiles,
creates `.claude/skills/**` links to `.agents/skills/**`, validates the copied
trees against their canonical sources, then atomically renames. It never
templates lockfiles, generated route trees, output, caches, or dependency trees.

Every scaffold includes the minimum repository-owned harness:

- fixed invariant and audit guidance inside the copied local skills;
- a repository harness profile as the sole local variation surface;
- one docs router and documentation owner map;
- structured audit scope, finding, and accepted-finding templates plus schemas;
- critical journeys, proof and bounded-receipt contracts;
- authority, feedback/control, automation, epoch, effectiveness, evidence, and
  runbook owners;
- deterministic governance and audit validation; and
- an active bootstrap-harness task that qualifies the rendered defaults before
  they become current repository truth.

The render receipt records official sources, selected versions, compatibility
decisions, config digests, limitations, and an explicitly absent lockfile. After
the first `bun install`, run `scripts/finalize_repository_receipt.py` to bind the
receipt to `bun.lock`; do not claim a bootstrapped fixture before that phase.

Use `--skills-root /absolute/skill-collection` only when the sibling skills are
installed outside the default collection. Generated repository-local skills
must remain useful without that global collection after rendering. Each copied
skill is the complete canonical folder. The docs-maintainer and
package-structure skills receive explicit generated repository profiles; those
profiles are the only permitted tree differences. Claude compatibility
surfaces are links, never independently maintained copies.

Include the complete `linear` skill because PRD Implementer loads it for
projects with Linear tracking. The generated receipt and local validator must
cover that folder and its Claude link too; a global installed copy does not
satisfy the generated repository's local references.

## Split folders and files by durable ownership

Choose paths from the call graph and semantic owner. A repository/package
boundary is justified by an independent contract; an app-internal subfolder is
justified by a durable capability, domain, adapter, authority, runtime, or
independently tested policy. File count alone is not a boundary, and a one-file
capability should stay a file when a folder would add no meaning.

- Start with actual callers, exports, tests, untrusted ingress, runtime
  composition, and provider/authority edges before moving a file.
- Name folders after capabilities/domains (`observability`, `cloudflare`, or
  `metrics-token-qualification`) and files after owned roles (`schemas.ts`,
  `errors.ts`, `service.ts`, `plan.ts`, `authority.ts`, `website.ts`, or
  `manifest.main.ts`).
- Do not scaffold every conventional file. Add `service.ts`, `live.layer.ts`,
  `test.layer.ts`, or `config.ts` only when a real service, resource Layer,
  deterministic test Layer, or durable configuration boundary exists.
- Keep tests beside app-internal owners or in the package's contract/test
  location; keep reusable fixtures in the package-approved testing owner.
  Reject `common/`, `shared/`, `helpers/`, and `utils/` dumping grounds.
- After a split, update imports, tests, architecture/README pointers, exports,
  and lifecycle/proof owners in the same slice. Preserve one canonical Schema,
  error, service, plan, and configuration owner.

## Enforce the separate Website/API architecture

Read the [TanStack, Effect and Alchemy architecture](references/tanstack-effect.md)
before composing apps. The scaffold uses the separate frontend/backend design:

- The domain package owns Schemas, failures, operations, source validation and
  live/test Layers. HTTP, RPC and optional MCP reuse that owner.
- apps/api composes the live domain and native handler Layers in Alchemy's
  instance Scope. Incoming work keeps the native request fibre and cleanup.
  It has no ManagedRuntime or extra Promise runner.
- apps/web remains a standard TanStack Website. Server loaders call the typed
  API through a private service binding; browser calls use their checked public
  API address. Do not bundle a backend fallback or machine routes into it.
- Keep one frontend server runner and one React-mounted browser Atom graph.
  No Effect Context, request-service merge or tracer-hook workaround goes
  through TanStack. Use matching server/client environment functions for imports.
- Native client Layers implement the domain contract, keep generated clients
  private, preserve checked named errors and enforce a whole-read deadline.
- One native Alchemy stack deploys both apps with a matching API per stage.
  Preview never connects to Production. Bind `Cloudflare.Worker.URL` for each
  host's own origin; use native resource Outputs for another host's address.
  Never hard-code or construct a deployed website address. Keep Schema checks
  where resolved bindings enter application code. A chosen custom domain is
  valid infrastructure input, not a second application origin setting. Follow
  the website origin rules in [Cloudflare](../alchemy-iac/references/providers/cloudflare.md).
- Every cross-workspace import uses explicit exports, including infrastructure.
- Routes and feature owners load data and choose error/workflow behaviour.
  Presentation components receive readonly values and action callbacks.
- Decode external input and encode outward values with their owning Schemas.
  Extract only demonstrated reuse, substantial work or a resource lifetime.

Check actual Worker startup after initialisation returns, response consumption
and cancellation, native-client errors and deadlines, real browser CORS and
bundle contents. Run negative Oxlint fixtures under the moved package paths;
a green typecheck or server call alone does not prove those connections.

## Add product analytics when required

For browser and backend PostHog analytics, read the
[application ownership and relay guide](../alchemy-iac/references/effect/posthog-analytics.md). It
routes to the Alchemy lifecycle and Effect browser adapter owners. Keep analytics
optional: the base scaffold does not provision projects or start collection.

## Verify and maintain

Run in this order:

```bash
bun install
bun run format:check
bun run lint
bun run test:lint-rules
bun run check-types
bun run test
bun run build
python3 scripts/validate_repository.py /absolute/repository
```

Inspect export consumers and generated docs in addition to command status. Read
[maintenance](references/maintenance.md) before changing versions, assets,
profiles, rules, or skill baselines. Report exact commands, exit codes, and any
blocked upstream incompatibility; do not waive a failing compatibility fixture.
Use the generated docs-maintainer owner map and lifecycle/skill checks for
documentation impact, and retain a bounded impact receipt with explicit
non-claims.

## Immutable Effect and Schema ownership

Apply the canonical strict-effect-ts policy to all owned TypeScript, including
tests, tools, configuration and infrastructure. Use immutable Effect Array,
Record, HashMap and HashSet operations and exhaustive Match. For pure work use
folds/unfolds; for effectful work use a bounded sequential traversal or owned
Stream. Ref belongs to real changing state with a pure immutable update.

Every meaningful identifier/value and data record has one owning Schema with
inferred types. Reuse fields, brands and whole-record checks across codecs;
decode actual external input/replies once, construct new constrained values
with checked constructors and named errors, and trust typed internal contracts.
Domain absence is Option. Preserve historical source formats, missing/null
distinctions and hashes when changing a codec. Internal caches use full readonly
address records, tested with installed equality/hash and cancellation rules.

Enable the portable no-imperative-collections rule alongside the existing
rules; prove it through actual negative and valid Oxlint fixtures in app,
package, tests, tools and config paths. Document precise host operation/property
allowances, never a whole-file or wildcard mutation waiver. Keep the native API
request execution and cleanup and the one exact TanStack server runner. Templates
are examples qualified at their snapshot; research a v4 clone and reconcile with
installed source/types before applying them to another Effect version.

# Strict Effect TypeScript

Treat Effect as the application language for every fallible, asynchronous, stateful, concurrent, resourceful, configuration-dependent, or boundary-crossing workflow. Allow plain TypeScript only for total, deterministic leaf computation and unavoidable host adapters.

Use this skill with repository-local instructions, `$repo-structure`, `$package-structure`, and `$effect-client-wrapper` where applicable. Use `$alchemy-iac` for infrastructure ownership, provider proof, and deployment lifecycle.

## Strictness level

This skill is intentionally stricter than ordinary Effect guidance.

In owned code, do not introduce:

- `async` or raw `Promise` orchestration;
- thrown domain or expected operational errors;
- raw `fetch` or an exposed SDK client;
- direct `process.env`, `Bun.env`, `import.meta.env`, or platform binding reads below a host adapter;
- unchecked `JSON.parse`, type assertions, `any`, or manual `unknown` narrowing;
- nullable domain models after ingress;
- `Date.now`, `new Date()` as a clock, `Math.random`, unmanaged timers, or sleeps;
- `console.*` for application telemetry;
- mutable local or global collections, loops, reassignment, raw `Map`/`Set`, or detached background work;
- repeated decoding of already checked domain values or JSON keys for an internal cache;
- copied primitive refinements or handwritten data types that compete with an owning Schema;
- generic callback escape hatches such as `request<T>(fn)`, `run<T>(callback)`, or `withClient(fn)`;
- package-owned runtimes or repeated `Effect.runPromise`;
- provider objects, wire DTOs, or primitive configuration crossing service boundaries.

A narrow host callback may be synchronous or Promise-shaped only when a framework requires it. Adapt it immediately to an Effect program, provide one application-owned runtime, and execute only at that boundary. Document any other exception beside the code with its host constraint, containment, and test.

## Allowed plain TypeScript

Keep plain TypeScript for:

- total pure functions over already-decoded values;
- type declarations and static constants;
- JSX and framework declarations that do not perform effects;
- immutable transformations using Effect Array, Record, HashMap and HashSet functions;
- the smallest adapter signature required by a host framework;
- performance-sensitive native data structures proven by measurement and encapsulated behind an Effect service.

Plain does not mean unchecked. Boundary data still requires Schema, failure still requires a typed error channel, and effects still require the application runtime.

Read [policy and exceptions](references/architecture/policy-and-exceptions.md).

## Mandatory workflow

### 1. Inspect the exact codebase

Before editing:

1. Read repository and package instructions.
2. Inspect the receiving repository's installed Effect version and exports. Research the cloned v4 source when available, record its revision, then check every chosen API against installed source/types and behaviour. The canonical template snapshot qualifies 4.0.2; it does not choose an upgrade for another repository.
3. Find existing schemas, errors, services, Layers, runtimes, test Layers, and observability.
4. Identify the current package boundary and intended public API.
5. Search the change surface for strictness violations.
6. Preserve unrelated dirty worktree changes.

When documentation and installed types disagree, follow the installed package, then record any compatibility decision.

### 2. Classify every operation

For each operation, identify:

- value success type;
- expected error union;
- service requirements;
- external inputs that need decoding;
- resource lifetime;
- concurrency and interruption behaviour;
- retry and timeout policy;
- logging, span, and metric semantics;
- runtime owner.

Use this translation:

| Vanilla TypeScript         | Required Effect model                                                                           |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `async` / `Promise`        | `Effect`, `Effect.gen`, `Effect.fn`; `tryPromise` only at ingress                               |
| `throw`                    | typed `Effect.fail`; defect only for impossible invariant failure                               |
| `T \| null \| undefined`   | decode once, then `Option<T>` where absence is semantic                                         |
| environment strings        | `Config` plus `Schema` refinement                                                               |
| JSON / `unknown`           | Schema decode and encode                                                                        |
| `fetch`                    | Effect Platform `HttpClient` or a private typed adapter                                         |
| provider SDK               | private `live.layer.ts`; decode every output                                                    |
| filesystem / child process | Effect Platform services in a private Layer                                                     |
| time / retry               | `Clock`, `Duration`, `Schedule`, timeout                                                        |
| randomness / identifiers   | Effect Random or an injected service                                                            |
| mutable state              | `Ref`, `SynchronizedRef`, `SubscriptionRef`; `TxRef` inside `Effect.tx` for coordinated updates |
| `Map` / `Set` domain state | `HashMap`, `HashSet`, `Chunk`, `ReadonlyArray`                                                  |
| event callback             | `Queue`, `PubSub`, `Deferred`, `Stream`                                                         |
| cleanup                    | `Scope`, acquire/use/release                                                                    |
| `console`                  | structured Effect logging                                                                       |
| test sleep / network       | `TestClock`, deterministic test Layer                                                           |

### 3. Model boundaries first

Create or update, in order:

1. `schemas.ts` for external and domain codecs, brands, and redaction policy.
2. `errors.ts` for the closed expected error vocabulary.
3. `service.ts` for named semantic operations.
4. `live.layer.ts` for SDK, transport, storage, and configuration wiring.
5. `memory.layer.ts` or a domain-specific test Layer with the identical contract.
6. operation modules only when they own substantial reusable policy.
7. an application runtime at the host root.

Do not create ceremonial files. A small service may colocate a coherent contract; split when ownership is stable. Read [file and package conventions](references/architecture/files-and-packages.md).

### 4. Make public operations closed

Declare owned Layers as static values. Their Requirements type channel names
the dependencies that callers must supply. Use native `Layer.succeed` at
composition sites and `Layer.mock` or replacement Layers in tests. Keep native
composition callbacks, but do not wrap a Layer in an owned factory function.
Enable the portable `strict-effect/static-layers` rule with the other Effect
checks; it has no factory exceptions or automatic fix.

A public service operation should normally have:

```ts
Effect.Effect<Success, DomainError, never>;
```

Build dependencies into the service Layer. Do not make each caller provide transport, configuration, clock, SDK, or persistence requirements unless the dependency is intentionally part of the public composition contract.

For fixed host settings, yield checked Config in the owning Layer; Config is
already yieldable. Use `Layer.unwrap` to configure existing Layers and
`Layer.effect` to construct a real service. Follow the
[configuration decision procedure](references/services/config-and-secrets.md)
before adding a Context service or options wrapper for a setting.

Expose named operations such as `createRedirectUri`, `queryDataset`, or `loadAccount`. Do not expose raw clients, arbitrary request methods, or generic callbacks.

Read [services and Layers](references/services/services-and-layers.md) and [provider adapters](references/services/provider-adapters.md).

### 5. Decode at ingress and encode at egress

- Decode environment, HTTP, queue, database, filesystem, provider, and state payloads immediately.
- Brand identifiers and constrained strings.
- Use exact object schemas where unknown keys would hide drift.
- Redact secrets at acquisition and in error/log encoders.
- Encode owned outbound payloads and durable receipts.
- Never cast a provider response into the domain type.
- Infer domain, service and wire data types from one owning Schema. Reuse its fields, brands and whole-record checks in transport and persistence codecs. Spreading fields does not copy a record-level check.
- Keep already decoded values typed through internal calls. Construct new constrained values with the owning fallible constructor and map its validation issue to a named error. Construct unchanged records directly from checked fields.
- Convert optional/null source fields into Option. When historical bytes distinguish missing keys from null, preserve that distinction in the codec and prove the original encoding and hashes.
- Use readonly structured cache keys with the installed equality/hash contract. Do not encode and decode internal keys as JSON.

Read [schemas and brands](references/modeling/schemas-and-brands.md), [errors and Causes](references/modeling/errors-and-causes.md), and [Config and secrets](references/services/config-and-secrets.md).

For Alchemy saved props and attributes, read
[checked stored values](references/modeling/alchemy-stored-values.md). Keep
optional fields encoded at their owner, preserve protected keys separately and
test historical readers against the actual selected state store and diff code.

### 6. Preserve structured effects

Keep Effect programs flat and sequential. Extract a helper only when it is independently reusable, represents stable policy, owns I/O, or owns resource lifetime.

Use structured concurrency. Every child fibre must be joined, scoped, supervised, or deliberately daemonised at an application boundary with an explicit lifecycle. Encode backpressure. Make interruption and finalisation part of the design.

Read [fibres, queues, and streams](references/concurrency/fibres-queues-and-streams.md) and [scope, time, retry, and interruption](references/concurrency/scope-time-retry-and-interruption.md).

### 7. Instrument semantic work

- Public service methods use named `Effect.fn("Service.operation")`.
- Short private pipelines stay plain functions. Dependent private generators
  use `Effect.fnUntraced` when they do not own a separate span. A private external
  operation may still deserve named `Effect.fn`. Do not add a generator only to
  wrap a direct pipeline.
- Log structured, bounded, secret-negative fields.
- Create spans around semantic operations and external calls, not Layer construction.
- Classify expected failure without dumping arbitrary Causes.
- Use low-cardinality metric labels.
- Add application/resource identity: service, version/revision, environment, stage, repository, and branch/ref where useful.
- Keep application telemetry separate from platform telemetry.
- Treat exporter success as transport evidence only; query the backend for ingestion proof.

Read [logging, tracing, and metrics](references/observability/logging-tracing-and-metrics.md).

### 8. Test the contract and its real boundary

Test:

- Schema boundary success and failure;
- each tagged error branch;
- Layer construction;
- live adapter translation using controlled transport or SDK fixtures;
- the same service contract through a memory/test Layer;
- timeout, retry, interruption, and cleanup using deterministic time;
- concurrency ordering and backpressure;
- observability field safety;
- serialisation round-trips.

Never make ordinary unit tests depend on the live network or wall-clock sleeps. Read [deterministic testing](references/testing/deterministic-testing.md).

### 9. Enforce the policy

Run narrow searches for forbidden constructs on changed owned TypeScript. Classify each match as:

- host-required adapter;
- generated/vendor code;
- measured encapsulated exception;
- violation.

Use lint restrictions, architecture tests, package exports, and code review to stop recurrence. Read [lint, review, and migration](references/enforcement/lint-review-and-migration.md).

## Domain reference map

Architecture:

- [policy and exceptions](references/architecture/policy-and-exceptions.md)
- [files and packages](references/architecture/files-and-packages.md)
- [runtimes and host boundaries](references/architecture/runtimes-and-boundaries.md)

Modelling:

- [schemas and brands](references/modeling/schemas-and-brands.md)
- [Alchemy saved values, legacy readers and protected secrets](references/modeling/alchemy-stored-values.md)
- [errors and Causes](references/modeling/errors-and-causes.md)
- [Option, Result, Match, and collections](references/modeling/option-either-match-and-collections.md)

Services and state:

- [services and Layers](references/services/services-and-layers.md)
- [Config and secrets](references/services/config-and-secrets.md)
- [provider adapters](references/services/provider-adapters.md)
- [state, collections, and caches](references/state/state-collections-and-caches.md)

Concurrency and resources:

- [fibres, queues, and streams](references/concurrency/fibres-queues-and-streams.md)
- [scope, time, retry, and interruption](references/concurrency/scope-time-retry-and-interruption.md)

Transports and persistence:

- [HTTP, RPC, and serialisation](references/transports/http-rpc-and-serialization.md)
- [filesystem, processes, and platform services](references/transports/filesystem-process-and-platform.md)
- [persistence and transactions](references/transports/persistence-and-transactions.md)

Observability and tests:

- [logging, tracing, and metrics](references/observability/logging-tracing-and-metrics.md)
- [deterministic testing](references/testing/deterministic-testing.md)

Applications:

- [Bun, CLI, workers, and framework hosts](references/applications/bun-cli-workers-and-frameworks.md)
- [browser and Web Platform](references/applications/browser-and-web-platform.md)
- [React and TanStack](references/applications/react-and-tanstack.md)
- [MCP and WebMCP](references/applications/mcp-and-webmcp.md)
- [PostHog browser service and scoped SDK adapter](../effect-client-wrapper/references/posthog-browser.md)
- [PostHog application, backend capture and native HTTP relay](../alchemy-iac/references/effect/posthog-analytics.md)

Enforcement and examples:

- [lint, review, and migration](references/enforcement/lint-review-and-migration.md)
- [strict cookbook](references/examples/strict-cookbook.md)
- [format-selected client contract](references/examples/format-selected-client.md)
- [anti-patterns](references/examples/anti-patterns.md)
- [primary sources and version policy](references/sources.md)

## Final review

Do not call the change strict Effect code unless all relevant statements are true:

- External data is decoded and outbound data is encoded.
- Expected failures are a closed tagged error union.
- Services expose named domain operations.
- Live dependencies are private to Layers.
- Public operations have no accidental requirements.
- Runtime execution occurs only at an application boundary.
- Time, randomness, retry, concurrency, state, and cleanup are Effect-managed.
- Nullable values do not leak past ingress.
- No raw client, generic callback, assertion, or Promise escape hatch was added.
- Logs, spans, metrics, and receipts are secret-negative and low-cardinality.
- Tests use deterministic Layers and prove failure/interruption paths.
- Pure work uses immutable Effect collection operations; changing shared state uses an owned Ref or transactional primitive with pure updates.
- Domain alternatives use exhaustive Match; Option and Result use their own matching APIs.
- Schemas and brands have one owner, typed internal calls do not decode again, and cache keys do not use JSON.
- Historical source formats, missing/null distinctions and byte hashes have explicit compatibility tests when changed.
- Any exception is narrow, documented, and enforced against expansion.

name: grilling
description: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
---

Interview the user relentlessly until you reach a shared understanding. Map this as a **design tree**: every decision branches into the decisions that hang off it.
Work the tree in **rounds**. The **frontier** is every decision whose prerequisites are already settled: the questions you can ask _now_ without guessing at answers you haven't heard yet. Ask the whole frontier in one round: number each question and give your recommended answer. Then wait for the user's answers before the next round.

Format a round like so:

```
❓ **Q1** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>

➡️ <your recommended answer>

---
❓ **Q2** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>

➡️ <your recommended answer>
```

Each round the user answers reshapes the tree: settled decisions push the frontier outward and unblock questions that depended on them. Recompute the frontier and ask the next round. A question whose answer depends on another question still open in this round belongs to a _later_ round, not this one.
Finding _facts_ is your job, never the user's. When a frontier question needs a fact from the environment (filesystem, tools, etc.), dispatch a sub-agent to find it; don't ask the user for anything you could look up yourself. Don't block on it: a running exploration is an unsettled prerequisite, so only the questions downstream of it wait for the sub-agent to report; ask the rest of the frontier now. The _decisions_ are the user's: put each to them and wait.
The session is done when the frontier is empty: every branch of the design tree visited, nothing left silently assumed. Do not act on it until the user confirms you have reached a shared understanding.

# Repository Structure

Create a small repository whose boundaries are executable, documented, and
updateable. Resolve current versions first; render only from a recorded snapshot.

## Audit before scaffolding

1. Read `AGENTS.md`, all repository-owned readable `docs/**` and `README*`,
   manifests, workspace/lock/runtime config, lint/format/test/CI config, skills,
   and representative apps/packages. Exclude generated, dependency, build, and
   vendored trees explicitly.
2. Inspect worktree state. For an existing repository, patch only authorized
   paths and preserve unrelated work.
3. For an existing-repository audit, read the
   [repository audit router](references/repository-audit.md), then load its
   [workflow](references/audit/workflow.md),
   [corpus and journeys](references/audit/corpus-and-journeys.md),
   [lenses](references/audit/lenses.md),
   [findings and acceptance](references/audit/findings-and-acceptance.md), and
   [variation and stopping](references/audit/variation-and-stopping.md).
   Then read the
   [repository contract](references/repository-contract.md),
   [TanStack and Effect architecture](references/tanstack-effect.md), and
   [tooling and docs](references/tooling-and-docs.md).
4. Load the canonical sibling
   [`package-structure`](../package-structure/SKILL.md) and
   [`docs-maintainer`](../docs-maintainer/SKILL.md) skills. Resolve them
   relative to this installed skill collection, or pass the skill collection
   explicitly to the renderer. Stop before rendering if either is unavailable;
   do not invent package/document contracts or assume a user's home directory.

## Audit an existing repository

Default to report-first. Define the target revision, claimed jobs, accepted
outcomes, proof boundaries, authority, exclusions, and stop conditions. Account
for the repository corpus, then follow a small set of representative jobs from
request through ownership, implementation, proof, delivery, and acceptance.
Use prior collaboration evidence when available and authorized; treat it as
trajectory evidence rather than repository policy.

For a whole-repository audit, create the structured scope and finding artifacts
from `assets/audit/`; do not use free-form prose as the sole audit record.
Validate them with `scripts/validate_audit_artifacts.py`. Return a
consequence-ordered Markdown view with stable IDs, separate important
corrections from optional improvements, identify the earliest owning
correction, and name duplicated machinery to retire. Stop for acceptance before
implementation unless the original request authorizes both. Record accepted
finding IDs in the crosswalk, hand them to `prd-writer`, then use `prd-review`
and `prd-implementer`.

For most repositories, stop after the structural and trajectory audit,
accepted important corrections, normal repository checks, and one fresh
independent review. Do not create a comparative harness evaluation unless the
claim is that a particular intervention changes future worker behavior.

## Resolve or select versions

Rendering is offline and deterministic. The checked-in snapshot is a known-good
fallback, not permission to call it current. To research a refresh, use primary
registries/official sources and DeepWiki only for upstream packages—not the
local codebase:

```bash
python3 scripts/resolve_versions.py --output /tmp/provisional-versions.json
```

Effect ecosystem packages share the qualified exact stable v4 version, currently
`4.0.2`. Resolve that exact version; registry `latest`/`beta` tags do not
select the qualified native Alchemy combination. TanStack Start and Router
resolve independently. Never emit `latest`.
Alchemy beta and the preview-only Cloudflare scaffold require an explicit
qualified/rejected decision; never infer compatibility from a registry tag.
Read [version policy](references/version-policy.md); a snapshot is adopted only
after full compatibility rendering and verification.

## Render safely

The target must be an absolute, new path. There is no overwrite mode:

```bash
python3 scripts/render_repository.py \
  --target /absolute/new/repository \
  --name example \
  --scope @example \
  --source-condition @example/source \
  --versions assets/version-snapshot.json
```

The renderer stages root/app/docs/tooling assets, invokes the canonical package
renderer for domain, RPC, and HTTP API packages, copies every complete current
repository-skill folder, adds only the declared repository-local profiles,
creates `.claude/skills/**` links to `.agents/skills/**`, validates the copied
trees against their canonical sources, then atomically renames. It never
templates lockfiles, generated route trees, output, caches, or dependency trees.

Every scaffold includes the minimum repository-owned harness:

- fixed invariant and audit guidance inside the copied local skills;
- a repository harness profile as the sole local variation surface;
- one docs router and documentation owner map;
- structured audit scope, finding, and accepted-finding templates plus schemas;
- critical journeys, proof and bounded-receipt contracts;
- authority, feedback/control, automation, epoch, effectiveness, evidence, and
  runbook owners;
- deterministic governance and audit validation; and
- an active bootstrap-harness task that qualifies the rendered defaults before
  they become current repository truth.

The render receipt records official sources, selected versions, compatibility
decisions, config digests, limitations, and an explicitly absent lockfile. After
the first `bun install`, run `scripts/finalize_repository_receipt.py` to bind the
receipt to `bun.lock`; do not claim a bootstrapped fixture before that phase.

Use `--skills-root /absolute/skill-collection` only when the sibling skills are
installed outside the default collection. Generated repository-local skills
must remain useful without that global collection after rendering. Each copied
skill is the complete canonical folder. The docs-maintainer and
package-structure skills receive explicit generated repository profiles; those
profiles are the only permitted tree differences. Claude compatibility
surfaces are links, never independently maintained copies.

Include the complete `linear` skill because PRD Implementer loads it for
projects with Linear tracking. The generated receipt and local validator must
cover that folder and its Claude link too; a global installed copy does not
satisfy the generated repository's local references.

## Split folders and files by durable ownership

Choose paths from the call graph and semantic owner. A repository/package
boundary is justified by an independent contract; an app-internal subfolder is
justified by a durable capability, domain, adapter, authority, runtime, or
independently tested policy. File count alone is not a boundary, and a one-file
capability should stay a file when a folder would add no meaning.

- Start with actual callers, exports, tests, untrusted ingress, runtime
  composition, and provider/authority edges before moving a file.
- Name folders after capabilities/domains (`observability`, `cloudflare`, or
  `metrics-token-qualification`) and files after owned roles (`schemas.ts`,
  `errors.ts`, `service.ts`, `plan.ts`, `authority.ts`, `website.ts`, or
  `manifest.main.ts`).
- Do not scaffold every conventional file. Add `service.ts`, `live.layer.ts`,
  `test.layer.ts`, or `config.ts` only when a real service, resource Layer,
  deterministic test Layer, or durable configuration boundary exists.
- Keep tests beside app-internal owners or in the package's contract/test
  location; keep reusable fixtures in the package-approved testing owner.
  Reject `common/`, `shared/`, `helpers/`, and `utils/` dumping grounds.
- After a split, update imports, tests, architecture/README pointers, exports,
  and lifecycle/proof owners in the same slice. Preserve one canonical Schema,
  error, service, plan, and configuration owner.

## Enforce the separate Website/API architecture

Read the [TanStack, Effect and Alchemy architecture](references/tanstack-effect.md)
before composing apps. The scaffold uses the separate frontend/backend design:

- The domain package owns Schemas, failures, operations, source validation and
  live/test Layers. HTTP, RPC and optional MCP reuse that owner.
- apps/api composes the live domain and native handler Layers in Alchemy's
  instance Scope. Incoming work keeps the native request fibre and cleanup.
  It has no ManagedRuntime or extra Promise runner.
- apps/web remains a standard TanStack Website. Server loaders call the typed
  API through a private service binding; browser calls use their checked public
  API address. Do not bundle a backend fallback or machine routes into it.
- Keep one frontend server runner and one React-mounted browser Atom graph.
  No Effect Context, request-service merge or tracer-hook workaround goes
  through TanStack. Use matching server/client environment functions for imports.
- Native client Layers implement the domain contract, keep generated clients
  private, preserve checked named errors and enforce a whole-read deadline.
- One native Alchemy stack deploys both apps with a matching API per stage.
  Preview never connects to Production. Bind `Cloudflare.Worker.URL` for each
  host's own origin; use native resource Outputs for another host's address.
  Never hard-code or construct a deployed website address. Keep Schema checks
  where resolved bindings enter application code. A chosen custom domain is
  valid infrastructure input, not a second application origin setting. Follow
  the website origin rules in [Cloudflare](../alchemy-iac/references/providers/cloudflare.md).
- Every cross-workspace import uses explicit exports, including infrastructure.
- Routes and feature owners load data and choose error/workflow behaviour.
  Presentation components receive readonly values and action callbacks.
- Decode external input and encode outward values with their owning Schemas.
  Extract only demonstrated reuse, substantial work or a resource lifetime.

Check actual Worker startup after initialisation returns, response consumption
and cancellation, native-client errors and deadlines, real browser CORS and
bundle contents. Run negative Oxlint fixtures under the moved package paths;
a green typecheck or server call alone does not prove those connections.

## Add product analytics when required

For browser and backend PostHog analytics, read the
[application ownership and relay guide](../alchemy-iac/references/effect/posthog-analytics.md). It
routes to the Alchemy lifecycle and Effect browser adapter owners. Keep analytics
optional: the base scaffold does not provision projects or start collection.

## Verify and maintain

Run in this order:

```bash
bun install
bun run format:check
bun run lint
bun run test:lint-rules
bun run check-types
bun run test
bun run build
python3 scripts/validate_repository.py /absolute/repository
```

Inspect export consumers and generated docs in addition to command status. Read
[maintenance](references/maintenance.md) before changing versions, assets,
profiles, rules, or skill baselines. Report exact commands, exit codes, and any
blocked upstream incompatibility; do not waive a failing compatibility fixture.
Use the generated docs-maintainer owner map and lifecycle/skill checks for
documentation impact, and retain a bounded impact receipt with explicit
non-claims.

## Immutable Effect and Schema ownership

Apply the canonical strict-effect-ts policy to all owned TypeScript, including
tests, tools, configuration and infrastructure. Use immutable Effect Array,
Record, HashMap and HashSet operations and exhaustive Match. For pure work use
folds/unfolds; for effectful work use a bounded sequential traversal or owned
Stream. Ref belongs to real changing state with a pure immutable update.

Every meaningful identifier/value and data record has one owning Schema with
inferred types. Reuse fields, brands and whole-record checks across codecs;
decode actual external input/replies once, construct new constrained values
with checked constructors and named errors, and trust typed internal contracts.
Domain absence is Option. Preserve historical source formats, missing/null
distinctions and hashes when changing a codec. Internal caches use full readonly
address records, tested with installed equality/hash and cancellation rules.

Enable the portable no-imperative-collections rule alongside the existing
rules; prove it through actual negative and valid Oxlint fixtures in app,
package, tests, tools and config paths. Document precise host operation/property
allowances, never a whole-file or wildcard mutation waiver. Keep the native API
request execution and cleanup and the one exact TanStack server runner. Templates
are examples qualified at their snapshot; research a v4 clone and reconcile with
installed source/types before applying them to another Effect version.
